title: The staff sign-in history is tested only for its happy path
what: The one test of the sign-in history walks a desk person through a wrong code, a sign-in, a save, a full download and a sign-out, and checks the five rows appear in order. It never checks that a wrong code keeps only the last four digits of the mobile, that removing a person writes a sign-out for each open device, that a member check-in or offer reward writes no save row, that the device name is cut to 80 letters, or that the apps have no right to read the raw history table.
expected: Each privacy rule of the sign-in history has a check: no full mobile kept, one sign-out per ended device, no rows for member-side saves, and the apps locked out of the table.
fix_line: Add checks for the masked mobile, the sign-out rows on removal, the member-side saves and the table rights

title: The nightly clean-up test never checks old support-access windows or delete requests
what: The clean-up test plants an old sign-in row, an old HQ audit row and an old creator address and checks they go. It plants no old support-access window and no delete request, so nothing checks that windows and finished delete requests older than 2 years are removed, or that an open delete request is kept. The clean-up is also never run twice in a row to check a retried night deletes nothing more and still succeeds.
expected: The test plants an old and a young support window, an old finished, an old cancelled and an open delete request, checks only the old finished ones go, and runs the clean-up a second time.
fix_line: Plant old and open support windows and delete requests in the clean-up test, and run it twice

title: Adding a staff person is never tested with wrong input or a mobile used before
what: The server tests add and remove people, and check the branch rules (desk elsewhere, removing yourself, the last owner). No server test tries a bad mobile, an empty name, an unknown role, a mobile already on the list or one person too many, and none checks a +91 or spaced mobile is stored as 10 digits. None adds back a person who was removed, so a wrong 'mobile already taken' for a removed person would pass. Nothing checks a removed person's unused sign-in codes are deleted.
expected: Each refusal when adding a person has a check, the mobile is stored clean, and adding back a removed person works as a fresh person with their old codes gone.
fix_line: Add server checks for each add-person refusal, the clean mobile, and adding a removed person back

title: Nothing checks another branch's desk cannot undo the home desk's visit or see a visitor's plan
what: The visitor test checks the desk sees a first name and not the surname or mobile, and that it can undo its own check-in. It never checks the answer leaves out the plan, payments and address, never has the home branch's own desk check a member in and then another branch try to undo it, and never checks a second check-in on the same day writes nothing new.
expected: The visitor answer is checked to hold only the five allowed fields, and an undo from another branch of a visit the home desk made is refused or leaves it in place.
who: owners with branches and their desks
fix_line: Check the visitor answer's exact fields and try an undo of a home-desk visit from another branch

title: Deleting a member's account is not checked to spare the gym's records or clear the profile
what: The member cloud test checks the copy rows and the sign-in account go when a member deletes the account. It never checks the member's summary and profile go too, never checks the gym's register, payments and check-ins for that member stay, and never checks the 'not signed in' answer or the last-saved time the app shows.
expected: Account deletion is checked to remove the summary and profile and to leave the gym's own records untouched; the SIGN_IN answer and lastSavedAt are checked.
fix_line: Add checks that deletion clears the profile and summary and leaves gym records, plus the SIGN_IN and last-saved answers

title: Renaming a business or a gym is never read back
what: The branch test renames the business and only checks the answer of that one call. The plans test renames a gym and only checks the call did not fail. Neither reads the name back, from another branch's list or from the gym itself, so a rename that saved nothing or renamed the wrong thing would pass.
expected: After a rename the new name is read back from every branch's list and from the gym.
fix_line: Read the new name back after each rename in the tests

title: No server test checks a gym keeps working after its free trial ends
what: The promise is that an ended trial only changes the words, never locks the gym. The only check is on the admin screen against a pretend server: the Add member button stays usable. No database test sets a gym's trial end in the past and then saves a member, a payment or a check-in, so a server rule that blocked an ended trial would go unnoticed. The audit row for a trial change is checked for its reason but not for the old and new end dates.
expected: A database test with a trial ended yesterday saves records and check-ins as normal, and the trial-change audit row is checked for its from and to dates.
fix_line: Add a database check that a gym past its trial still saves, and check the audit's from and to dates

title: Nothing checks the terms acceptance survives the owner who accepted being removed
what: The terms test checks the acceptance cannot be edited or deleted, and goes when the gym is deleted. It never removes the owner who accepted, so nothing checks the row stays with the name kept and only the person link cleared.
expected: Removing the person who accepted leaves the acceptance row, with the name kept and the person link empty.
fix_line: Remove the accepting owner in the test and read the acceptance row back
